title: Closing the Loop
summary: Linked automations create a complete customer journey and provide data that informs Analyst decisions.

sections.heading: Orientation
sections.subtitle: Introduction
sections.contentMarkdown:
- What will you understand? Powerful standalone automations — but when linked in a single Customer Journey, they become a system.
- Why now? After gathering leads, WhatsApp, and follow-ups, you need the complete picture, not just individual parts.
- What comes after the lesson? You will map a journey from start to finish, from lead to follow-up.

sections.heading: Tension
sections.subtitle: A Familiar Situation
sections.contentMarkdown:
- Everything works — but there is no complete picture.
- You have a form capturing leads. WhatsApp responds. Follow-ups send messages. Each one works.
- But you don’t know: Which channel brings in the best leads? Which follow-up message gets the most responses? Where does the customer drop off?
- Standalone automations without linking = a lot of work without learning. Linking generates data — and that data leads you to the Analyst path.

sections.heading: Core Idea
sections.subtitle: One Journey = Lead → Response → Follow-up → Data
sections.contentMarkdown:
- Lead capture: Grabs attention and records it.
- WhatsApp / Instant Response: Serves the customer confidently.
- Follow-up: Continues the conversation if it goes silent.
- Each step records: Source, Time, Channel, Response, Conversion. This is what the Analyst reads.

sections.heading: Comparison
sections.subtitle: Standalone Islands vs. Connected Journey
sections.contentMarkdown:
| Standalone Automations | One Customer Journey |
|-----------------------|---------------------|
| The form works, WhatsApp works, follow-ups work — but there is no map. "What was useful?" — No answer. | Lead from ad → Registration → WhatsApp response → Follow-up on days 2 and 5 → Conversion or closure. Each step is recorded — you can ask and improve.

sections.heading: Glossary
sections.subtitle: Two Terms for Linking
sections.contentMarkdown:
| Term | Meaning | Example |
|------|---------|---------|
| Customer Journey | The complete path from initial interest to follow-up or purchase — not just one step | Ad → Form → Welcome → Follow-up → Sales Call |
| Feedback Loop | The data recorded by the automation returns to inform you on what to improve | "Follow-up on day 2 via WhatsApp opened 40% response — day 5 email opened 10%" |

sections.heading: Screenshot Block
sections.contentMarkdown: Each stage feeds into the next and records data. The connected journey = questions that the Analyst will answer.

sections.heading: Quiz
sections.subtitle: Quick Confirmation
sections.contentMarkdown:
Question: You have leads from 3 channels and follow-ups are working — but you don’t know which channel brings in customers who buy. What is the best question to ask the data?
Which channel brought in leads that converted at the highest rate?
Explanation: The connected journey allows you decision-making questions — not just counting. Channel + conversion = Analyst.

sections.heading: Mission
sections.subtitle: Map the Lead to Follow-up Journey
sections.contentMarkdown:
Introduction: The mission is a journey map — not a technical audit. Connect what you’ve learned: Capture, Response, Follow-up — in one customer path. No real numbers are needed — just 5-6 stages + one Analyst question. Submission: Lead source · Stages 1-4 (Capture, Response, Follow-up, End) · One Analyst question · Sentence: What was missing before linking? Evaluation Criteria: | Dimension | Weight | Criteria |
|-----------|--------|----------|
| Connected Journey | 60% | 5 linked stages — not standalone automations |
| Analyst Bridge | 40% | One decision question based on journey data |
